reason: B is the stronger proposal because it extends prior magnesium-perrhenate additive results to a testable solid coating on HEAs and directly targets room-to-high-temperature operation, whereas A largely repeats the cited nanoflake spray-coating study and relies on ethanol-derived amorphous carbon that is unlikely to persist in oxidative high-temperature service. B remains speculative because coating adhesion and perrhenate stability/reaction products at 600–800 °C are not established, but its proposed experiment can decisively test those issues.
